head: ba457bf

scan_coverage.inferential_review: complete over the 14 changed production files plus exposition-sink neighbours
scan_coverage.runtime_exploitation: live uvicorn on port 8035, default (httptools) and --http h11 protocols, server killed after the run

closed_since_round_2.title: /metrics Prometheus exposition injection
closed_since_round_2.evidence: 9 hostile paths (quote, LF, CR, CRLF+forged series, backslash, braces, NUL, TAB, ESC) produced 0 forged series and 0 raw control characters; slo-check.js reported verdict=pass, error_rate_pct=0, p95_ms=4.75 (round 2: 99.90%)

closed_since_round_2.title: /metrics unbounded cardinality via the route label
closed_since_round_2.evidence: 20,000 distinct paths on one keep-alive connection added exactly 1 series line (555 -> 556) and 0.7 MB RSS; the new _duration_counts/_duration_totals share the same bounded (method, route) key

closed_since_round_2.title: HTTPException.headers discarded
closed_since_round_2.evidence: 405 returns Allow: GET, 401 returns WWW-Authenticate: Bearer; 404/422/500 all return the envelope with X-Request-ID

closed_since_round_2.title: sanitise_context skipped scrub_text for int/bool values and for mapping keys
closed_since_round_2.evidence: registered 12-digit Aadhaar redacted as int, Decimal, dict key, lowercase PAN and spaced form; float dropped; nested dict/list/bytes/None dropped; a __str__ that raises is dropped without propagating

findings.description: The `method` label on both the RED counter and the new duration histogram is taken raw from the ASGI scope with no allow-list and no length cap; the only bound is httptools' method table. Under uvicorn's pure-Python fallback (--http h11) 20,000 requests with distinct 67-character methods on one keep-alive connection grew the exposition from 79 lines / 85 KB to 300,094 lines / 42,186,513 bytes and retained +16.5 MB RSS; a single 5,000-character method adds ~75 KB permanently and is re-served on every public /metrics scrape.
findings.refutation_attempted: Under this repo's own dependency set (uvicorn[standard] -> httptools 0.8.0) and documented run command, unknown/overlong methods are rejected with 400 before the ASGI app runs - verified for unknown, 300-char and 5,000-char methods. That configuration-level mitigation is why this is medium and not high.
findings.escalation_trigger: E15-S2 shipping a Dockerfile that installs uvicorn without the `standard` extra, or any deployment passing --http h11
findings.fix: Bucket the method label through an application-level allow-list in middleware.py, mapping anything else to a single `<other>` bucket.

findings.description: The inbound X-Request-ID is accepted with no charset or length validation, then reflected on the response and embedded in every JSON log line. Measured: a 5,000,000-byte id produced a 5,000,219-byte response and wrote 5,000,148 bytes to the log sink from one unauthenticated request (~30,000x amplification vs the 164-byte baseline). A PAN-format id is accepted, echoed and logged unredacted because it is never registered as sensitive. CR/LF/NUL are rejected by the HTTP parser, so no response-splitting path exists.
findings.fix: Accept only ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$ on entry; otherwise generate a fresh id.

findings.description: sanitise_context scrubs keys but applies neither drop rule to them: the credential-URI pattern and the 200-character cap live in _sanitise_value, which runs on values only. Verified: a DSN carrying an inline password is dropped as a value but egresses whole as a key; a 5,000-character key egresses at full length; control characters in a key egress (JSON-escaped).
findings.refutation_attempted: context is developer-supplied and no production code raises AppError yet, so nothing attacker-controlled reaches a key at HEAD - hence medium, not high.
findings.fix: Run keys through the same gate as values, with a short length cap and an identifier charset.

findings.description: The redaction pattern tolerates only space/tab/hyphen separators and does no normalisation, so dot-separated, NBSP, zero-width-space and fullwidth-digit forms of a registered 12-digit Aadhaar all pass through unredacted (spaced and lowercase forms do redact).
findings.refutation_attempted: Commit ba457bf touched only specs/bundles/*, specs/stories/* and harness state - no backend file. A grep of backend/src confirms zero register_sensitive/redact_values call sites in production code, so no real PII is registered today and the bypass remains latent. Not escalated this round.
findings.escalation_trigger: the first production register_sensitive call site (E4-S1 POST /applications, E1-S1 POST /auth/login) - at that point this becomes high
findings.fix: NFKC-normalise and strip separators/zero-width characters on both pattern and haystack.

findings.description: _redaction_pattern is an lru_cache(maxsize=256) keyed on the sensitive value, and the compiled pattern embeds it. Verified: after the request-scoped redaction set is torn down the cache still returns the same compiled object for the PII key and the value is recoverable from pattern.pattern, so up to 256 PANs/Aadhaars persist for the process lifetime despite the docstring's request-scoped claim.
findings.fix: Key the cache on a salted digest of the value, or compile per scope.

findings.description: No security response headers are set anywhere. A live GET /health returns only date, server, content-length, content-type and x-request-id - no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy or Strict-Transport-Security.
findings.fix: Add a header middleware inside CorrelationIdMiddleware in create_app.

findings.description: Starlette's default redirect_slashes builds the redirect target from the untrusted Host header: GET /health/ with Host: evil.example returned 307 with location: http://evil.example/health, verified over a raw socket.
findings.fix: Add TrustedHostMiddleware with an allow-list from Settings, and/or redirect_slashes=False.

findings.description: /docs and /openapi.json both return 200 unauthenticated. /docs is HTML that loads Swagger UI CSS/JS from cdn.jsdelivr.net with no CSP and no SRI, so a CDN compromise executes script in the application origin; /openapi.json will enumerate every guarded route from group B onward.
findings.fix: Gate both behind an environment flag or the E1-S1 auth layer, and self-host the Swagger assets.

findings.description: /metrics is unauthenticated. Judged as a deferral rather than a fresh finding per E15-S4's Scope Out: what it exposes at HEAD is the route inventory, per-method/route/status counts and latency distributions - no PII, secrets or tenant data - so deferring auth to the api-contracts.md amendment plus E1-S1 is defensible. Two conditions: the endpoint is also the amplification surface in SEC2-W1, and an interim mitigation (bind or firewall the scrape path, or gate on a settings flag) needs no contract change.
findings.fix: Land auth or a bind-scope restriction with E1-S1; do not defer past it.

findings.description: The thousands-separator lookahead in Money.format() is quadratic. Timed on the regex alone (no toFixed in the measured region): 1,000 digits 0.5 ms, 4,000 5.7 ms, 16,000 100.8 ms, 32,000 417.1 ms, 100,001 digits 4,116.5 ms - a clean 4x per doubling. MoneyText accepts a raw string prop and calls Money.fromWire with no magnitude bound.
findings.refutation_attempted: No reachable path from attacker-controlled input at HEAD: MoneyText has no consumer anywhere in frontend/src, and the backend cannot emit such a value - Money.__init__/_quantize reject anything beyond the 28-digit decimal context (1e100 and 1e26+2dp both raise InvalidMoneyAmountError). Hence medium rather than high.
findings.fix: Bound the magnitude in toQuantizedDecimal and/or group digits with a linear loop.

findings.description: npm audit at HEAD: critical vitest (arbitrary file read via the UI server / @vitest/mocker), high vite (path traversal in optimized deps), moderate esbuild, vite-node, @vitest/mocker. All five resolve to devDependencies; production deps are decimal.js, react and react-dom with no advisories. Kept at medium rather than info because the critical one is a live developer-workstation exposure while the test/dev server listens.
findings.fix: Bump vite and vitest to the patched versions and re-run npm audit.

findings.description: _LABEL_ESCAPES covers backslash, double quote and newline only - carriage return and every other C0 control character pass through unescaped. No channel delivers one at HEAD (method is parser-validated on both protocol implementations and route templates are developer-controlled), so this is defence in depth rather than an exploitable hole.
findings.fix: Escape or strip the whole \x00-\x1f range in _escape_label.

findings.description: handle_validation_error echoes no rejected value, but with extra="forbid" the offending field NAME is attacker-supplied and is reflected verbatim and uncapped into the envelope: a probe with a script-tag field name returned {"field":"body.<script>...</script>"} as application/json. No execution is demonstrable (JSON is not rendered as HTML by current browsers), but there is no nosniff header (SEC2-W6) and no length cap (SEC2-W3).
findings.fix: Cap the field length and restrict it to an identifier charset before it enters the envelope.

findings.description: Money.multiply catches only InvalidOperation, so decimal.Overflow escapes untyped - verified with a 10**999999 scalar. Any service passing an attacker-influenced scalar yields an unhandled ArithmeticError and a 500. No information leak: the 500 envelope was verified clean through the real middleware chain.
findings.fix: Catch DecimalException (or ArithmeticError) and re-raise as InvalidMoneyAmountError.

findings.description: The line regex matches the label block as \{[^}]*\} and is not quote-aware, so any series whose route label contains a closing brace - i.e. every parameterized template such as /applications/{application_id}, arriving with group B - fails the match and is silently skipped, removing its counts and latency buckets from slo-check.js's error-rate and p95 with no warning. Harness-side and not attacker-reachable, but it is this gate's own measurement path.
findings.fix: Make the label-block match quote-aware, or fail loudly on an unparsed non-comment line.

findings.description: No throttling on any endpoint. Group A ships no login/reset/OTP route so there is nothing to brute-force yet, but SEC2-W1 and SEC2-W2 are both amplification findings a limiter would blunt.
findings.fix: Land a limiter with the E1-S1 auth layer; exempt /health and /metrics deliberately.

findings.description: Every response carries `server: uvicorn`, disclosing the server stack.
findings.fix: Run with --no-server-header or strip the header in the header middleware.

findings.description: gitleaks, semgrep and pip-audit are unprovisioned, so the SAST, secrets-history and Python-dependency tiers are UNSCANNED this round. My inferential pass over the 14 changed files found no hardcoded credential, no eval/exec/subprocess/pickle/yaml.load, no raw SQL, no innerHTML/dangerouslySetInnerHTML and no direct os.environ/process.env read (settings come from pydantic-settings with the TRUELEND_ prefix).
findings.fix: Provision the three scanners so these classes get tool coverage rather than review coverage.

findings.description: PAN/Aadhaar-shaped fixture values appear in tests only; none is used in production config. Recorded per the standing test-fixture convention.
findings.fix: None required.

findings.description: slo-verdict.json is written by slo-check.js and was overwritten by a concurrent sibling instance (port 8036) after my own port-8035 run; I deliberately did not restore it. Treat the file as unreliable evidence for this round - my measurement (verdict pass, error_rate 0%, p95 4.75 ms) is recorded in the prose report instead.
findings.fix: Have concurrent gate instances write instance-suffixed sensor verdicts, as the review reports already do.

not_tested: gitleaks / semgrep / pip-audit - absent from the environment
container and compose posture (deployed protocol choice, reverse-proxy header caps, TLS/HSTS) - no Dockerfile or docker-compose.yml exists at HEAD
auth bypass / IDOR / privilege escalation / CSRF - no authenticated or state-changing route exists in group A
real log-rotation behaviour behind SEC2-W2 - no rotation policy in the repo
time-to-outage under sustained load - amplification factors measured, no load harness run
